title: Preserve arc geometry in PCB board outlines and cutouts
description: Preserves arc geometry in PCB board outlines and cutouts by reusing the existing BRep point_with_bulge schema, preventing loss of circular arc data during KiCad export.
body:
Parsing PCB board outlines and cutouts currently strips `bulge`, losing the original circular arc before KiCad export. Once only endpoints or sampled points remain, the exporter cannot reliably recover the authored curve.

Reuse the existing BRep `point_with_bulge` schema and `PointWithBulge` type for `pcb_board.outline`, polygon cutout `points`, and slot cutout `route`. This preserves the arc data while keeping existing point-only inputs valid.

Prior work: [#711 — Represent PCB path arcs with bulges](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/711) proposes the same representation for trace and graphic paths. It does not cover board outlines or cutouts. This PR fills that gap and targets `main` independently. Producer and KiCad exporter changes remain follow-up work.

Arc convention:

- Points use board coordinates in millimetres, with +X right and +Y up.
- `bulge = tan(signed_sweep_radians / 4)` describes the circular arc from a point to the next. Positive is counterclockwise; negative is clockwise. Zero or omission means a straight segment.
- Board outlines and polygon cutouts are closed: the final point connects to the first. Slot paths are open: the final point has no outgoing segment.

Validation:

- All three new regression tests fail on the original schemas because arc bulges are stripped, and pass with this change.
- `bun test`: 546 passed, covering rounded board corners, clockwise circular cutouts, and a major arc followed by a straight slot segment.
- Type checking, ESM/declaration build, Zod lint, snake-case checks, and Biome checks on changed files pass.

title: RFC: store per-net PCB trace clearance on source_net
description: Proposes the Circuit JSON contract for per-net PCB trace clearance by storing the authoring value on source_net.min_trace_clearance as an optional finite, nonnegative number in millimeters.
body:
Proposes the Circuit JSON contract for per-net PCB trace clearance. Store the authoring value on `source_net.min_trace_clearance` as an optional finite, nonnegative number in millimeters. Keep the field absent when the author omits it. An explicit zero adds no clearance above the applicable existing minimum.

### Pair rule

Measure the shortest copper-edge-to-copper-edge gap on a shared copper layer between different electrical nets. The rule covers trace–trace, trace–pad, and trace–via copper pairs, including fixed traces and the copper on layers spanned by a via. Use the existing rules for pairs outside that scope.

For each applicable pair, take the maximum of the existing clearance for that pair and the values on both electrical nets. A missing value contributes zero. Use electrical connectivity to identify each net. If multiple `source_net` records resolve to the same electrical net, take the largest declared value across those records. With an existing minimum of 0.10 mm and net minima of 0.15 mm and 0.25 mm, the required gap is 0.25 mm regardless of which side has the trace.

### Downstream contract

- Core copies the parsed `<net minTraceClearance="0.25mm" />` value into this field.
- The autorouter needs the per-net values and matching electrical net IDs for route connections and existing copper, including nets with no pending connections. Checks reads the same requirement from saved Circuit JSON and evaluates the finished copper independently.
- A small integration repro can declare two nets and fixed copper directly in the TSX test body. With the values above, a 0.20 mm gap should flag a clearance violation and the router should find a path with at least 0.25 mm of clearance when room exists.

The schema test covers omission, zero, JSON round-tripping, and rejection of negative, non-finite, and nonnumeric values. Named net classes and class-to-class rules are tracked in [tscircuit#5808](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5808) and [Checks #550](https://github.com/tscircuit/checks/pull/550).

title: Add assembly.sticker props
description: Adds assemblyProps.sticker for an assembly.sticker  element, allowing users to apply adhesive stickers to parts in their assemblies.
body:
Adds `assemblyProps.sticker` for an `<assembly.sticker />` element: an adhesive sticker applied to one surface of its parent part. Props only; core still has to register the element and emit Circuit JSON (proposed in tscircuit/circuit-json#1018).

```tsx
<assembly.printedpart name="LID" jscad={<Lid />}>
  <assembly.sticker
    name="LABEL"
    imageUrl="./label.svg"
    surfaceRef="topSurface"
    width="36mm"
    height="17mm"
  />
</assembly.printedpart>
```

It is a child of `assembly.part` or `assembly.printedpart` and is positioned exactly like a laser engraving, reusing `ManufacturingSurfacePlacementProps`. It sits in the `assembly` namespace and takes BOM props because, unlike an engraving, it is a separate purchased item.

## Accepted inputs, output and defaults

| Prop | Accepted input | Parsed output | Omission |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | Nonblank string | Trimmed | Rejected |
| `displayName` | String | Unchanged | Absent |
| `imageUrl` | Nonempty URL string or static-file import | String | Absent; an unprinted sticker |
| `width`, `height` | Finite positive mm number or distance string | Number in mm | With `imageUrl`, one may be absent and follows the image's aspect ratio. Without it, both are required |
| `thickness` | Finite positive mm number or distance string | Number in mm | Absent; no thickness is assumed |
| `backgroundColor` | Nonblank string | Trimmed | Absent |
| `surfaceRef`, offsets, edge distances, `anchorAlignment`, `rotationOnSurface` | Same as `manufacturing.laserengraving.*` | Same | `surfaceRef` rejected; `anchorAlignment` defaults to `"center"` |
| `supplierPartNumbers`, `purchaseUrls` | Same as other assembly parts | Same | Absent |

There are no aliases. The change is additive, so nothing migrates; old core versions ignore the element.

## Conflicts

- Two position props on one axis are rejected, as for engravings.
- Giving both `width` and `height` with an `imageUrl` stretches the artwork to that size.

## Open questions

- **Child or sibling.** The laser engraving proposal suggested a sticker might instead be a sibling part attached with `mountedTo`. This PR makes it a child with `surfaceRef` because face mounting has no edge distances or rotation on the surface, and would need a `mountFace` that a sticker does not have.
- **Shape and stock.** Rectangles only. Corner radius, die-cut outlines, material and finish are left out.

title: RFC: add minTraceClearance to net props
description: Proposes the optional minTraceClearance?: Distance prop on net.
body:
Proposes the optional `minTraceClearance?: Distance` prop on `<net>`.

```tsx
<net name="USB_DP" minTraceClearance="0.15mm" />
<net name="RF_SIGNAL" minTraceClearance="0.25mm" />
```

The shared distance parser normalizes numbers in millimeters and unit strings such as `"10mil"` to finite, nonnegative millimeters. Omission leaves the value undefined.

The value applies to the copper-edge gap between a trace and a different net’s trace, pad, or via on a shared layer. The required gap is the largest of the applicable existing minimum and the two nets’ values. Core can copy the parsed value directly to `source_net.min_trace_clearance`.

Tests cover omission, numeric millimeters, unit conversion, zero, and invalid values. The Circuit JSON companion carries the consumer contract and the routing/DRC acceptance case. [Circuit JSON proposal](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/1019)

title: feat: propose manufacturing.laserengraving text and image props
description: Proposes a manufacturing namespace with two elements for laser-engraved marks on a part surface. They are children of assembly.printedpart or assembly.part. Elements are named for the process, so a mark says how it is made and not only how it looks.
body:
Proposes a `manufacturing` namespace with two elements for laser-engraved marks on a part surface. They are children of `assembly.printedpart` or `assembly.part`. Elements are named for the process, so a mark says how it is made and not only how it looks.

```tsx
<assembly.printedpart name="LID" jscad={<Lid />} material="petg">
  <manufacturing.laserengraving.text
    text="REV B"
    surfaceRef="topSurface"
    fontSize="3mm"
    distanceFromSurfaceLeftEdge="4mm"
    distanceFromSurfaceTopEdge="4mm"
  />
  <manufacturing.laserengraving.image
    imageUrl="./logo.svg"
    surfaceRef="badge"
    width="18mm"
    rotationOnSurface="90deg cw"
  />
</assembly.printedpart>
```

## What's in it

- **Surface.** `surfaceRef` is required: a built-in bounding surface (`topSurface`, `bottomSurface`, `leftSurface`, `rightSurface`, `frontSurface`, `backSurface`) or a named reference surface on the parent part.
- **Position.** At most one prop per axis, in the surface's frame: `xOffsetFromSurfaceCenter`, `distanceFromSurfaceLeftEdge`, `distanceFromSurfaceRightEdge`, and the same three for Y. An axis with none is centered. `anchorAlignment` picks the mark's anchor point. `rotationOnSurface` takes degrees or a string such as `"90deg ccw"` or `"90deg cw"`.
- **Laser engraving.** `engravingDepth` and `resultingColor` on both elements; `text`, `fontSize`, `font`, `textStyle` on text; `imageUrl`, `width`, `height`, `rasterMode`, `invertImage` on image.
- **Registry.** `manufacturingProps.laserengraving.text` and `.image`, mirroring `enclosureProps.fdm.box`.

The full contract (accepted inputs, parsed output, defaults, conflicts, core acceptance cases) is in `docs/proposals/manufacturing-laserengraving.md`.

## Reference surface `outwardNormal`

`assembly.referencesurface` gains `outwardNormal`, the direction a surface faces; a mark is engraved on and seen from that side. `normalDirection` remains as an alias with the same meaning. Giving both with different values is rejected, and parsed output carries both names with the same value, so current core keeps working.

## Shared rotation parser

`rotationOnSurface` uses a new `lib/common/rotation` parser, which now also backs `pcbRotation`, `schRotation`, `schematicrect`'s `rotation` and the KiCad footprint `rotation`.

- **Accepted.** A number in degrees, or `"<n>"`, `"<n>deg"` or `"<n>rad"` with an optional `ccw` or `cw`. Parsed to degrees counterclockwise.
- **Behavior change.** `"90deg cw"` used to parse to `90` because the direction was ignored; it is now `-90`. Strings outside the grammar (for example `"90 degrees"`) and non-finite numbers used to parse leniently or to `NaN`; they are now rejected.
- **Unchanged.** Bend angles, arc angles and source phases keep the circuit-json parser.

Every rotation string in tscircuit/core's lib, tests and docs (`"270deg"`, `"90deg"`, `"-90"`, `"45"` and similar) fits the new grammar.

## Open questions

- **"Top" means +Z here.** Board edges use `topedge` for +Y and the face-mounting proposal calls +Y "top" and +Z "above". The alternative is `aboveSurface`/`belowSurface`.
- **Built-in surfaces need part bounds.** Imported models have `modelBounds`, but `jscad` parts are emitted as a plan without evaluating geometry, so core has to evaluate bounds or leave built-in surfaces for the consumer to resolve.
- **Machine settings** (power, speed, pass count) are left out.

## Notes

- Props only. Nothing renders until core supports these elements.
- `generated/PROPS_OVERVIEW.md` also picks up `PcbDriverReceiverChannelProps` and `SimulationEyeDiagramProps`, which were missing from the generated file on main.

On this SEPIC board, requesting either 0.25 mm or 0.50 mm produces identical routing input with `minTraceToPadEdgeClearance: 0.1`. title: chore: bump autorouter to 0.0.1128 and fanout solver to 0.0.86
description: Updates the autorouter and fanout solver dependencies to their latest versions, ensuring compatibility and improved functionality in routing and clearance checks.
body:
Bump `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` to `^0.0.1128` for tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3939, which checks direct and inset routes against neighboring pads and removes the captured A13 BALL_C3 contact. Both npm releases and their merged source contents are verified. Bus-lanes-solver is current at `0.0.62`.

The A13 D0–D3 fixture is a negative case for the configured **0.2 mm** clearance. Its known DRAM_D3 finding moves from U200.BALL_F9 (0.088046 mm) to U200.BALL_E9 (0.078536 mm). Remove the incidental 0.08 mm bounds on previously observed failing output; they were introduced to characterize that output, and are not board design rules. Keep the bounded known 0.2 mm violations, connectivity, no drilled pads, and all other physical checks. Explicitly reject trace/pad and via/pad overlap with zero-clearance checks. The separate eighteen-path A13 fixture still requires zero DRC findings at 0.2 mm.

Refresh affected routing snapshots, including A13, RP2040 saved-path replay, INA237 pin attribution, Watchy, and the regulator breakout. Resolve main’s fanout-version conflict by preserving `0.0.86` and core’s current version.

title: Keep small-board mouse bites drillable (#5066)
description: Adjusts mouse-bite drill sizes for small boards to ensure they remain drillable according to JLCPCBs specifications, while addressing clearance issues with traces.
body:
**Stack:** 2/2, #5492, the repro → this fix. Merge #5658 first, then merge this into the repro branch, then merge #5492 (now containing the fix) to `main`.

**Depends on #5658**, which bumps `@tscircuit/jlcpcb-manufacturing-specs` to the release with `jlcPanelRules`. This branch includes that bump, so `package.json` shows it here until #5658 merges.

**JLCPCB rules:** the minimums now come from `jlcPanelRules` instead of hardcoded numbers:
- `MIN_MOUSE_BITE_DIAMETER` = `jlcPanelRules.min_non_plated_hole_diameter` (0.5 mm, JLCPCB's minimum non-plated hole)
- `MIN_MOUSE_BITE_SPACING` = `jlcPanelRules.recommended_mouse_bite_spacing.max` (0.3 mm, the stronger end of JLCPCB's recommended 0.2–0.3 mm)

The values are unchanged, so no snapshots move.

Stacked on #5492. Fixes the small-board case of #5066. **Draft for review:** it includes a tradeoff, described below.

Tabs shrink on small boards, and the mouse-bite drills used to shrink with them, down to 0.27 mm drills at a 0.405 mm pitch. `getMouseBiteSize` in `lib/utils/panels/generate-panel-tabs-and-mouse-bites.ts` now has two named minimums:
- `MIN_MOUSE_BITE_DIAMETER`: a 0.5 mm drill
- `MIN_MOUSE_BITE_SPACING`: a 0.3 mm web between holes

That gives a 0.8 mm pitch on small boards, the "about 0.5 mm holes at about 0.8 mm pitch" asked for in the issue. Boards whose scaled drill is already above the minimums don't change. The issue's 14 × 18 mm example keeps 0.63 mm drills at a 0.945 mm pitch.

**Repro.** The test is unchanged. In its snapshots, the first two drills go from 0.27 mm at a 0.405 mm pitch to 0.5 mm at a 0.8 mm pitch. Each tab now has one row of drills on the board edge. The second row on the far side of the 0.6 mm slot is dropped, because it would sit closer than the minimum pitch to the first row.

**Other snapshots updated by the larger drills:**
- `panel-with-tabs` (custom props)
- `panel-traces-routing-bounds`
- `subpanel13`
- `repro80-tab-routing-too-big` (both snapshots)

**Tradeoff to review: repro86.** Its boards are only 2 mm tall. A 0.5 mm drill centred on the board edge now comes within 0.166 mm of the R1–R2 trace, and the required clearance is 0.2 mm. The test used to assert zero errors. It now expects 32 `pcb_trace_error`s and snapshots the message. The issue asked for exactly this: holes kept clear of copper, "or at least a warning". Alternatives, if you'd rather avoid the errors:
- Move the drills outward so they reach less far into the board.
- Allow drills below 0.5 mm on very small tabs.

All 123 panel tests and the typecheck pass locally.

title: fix: round-trip branched saved routing phases
description: Fixes saved-phase failures by ensuring complete phases validate copper connectivity for export and replay, allowing shared anchor pads and junctions while rejecting cross-net connections.
body:
Fixes the saved-phase failures reproduced in #5643. Complete phases now use physical copper connectivity to validate both export and replay. A path can share an anchor pad or meet another path at a same-layer junction. Each requested connection still has to be covered, and copper that joins different electrical nets is rejected.

Export keeps the solver’s route order and chooses a port from the connected copper as the frame for `pcbTracePaths`. Replay resolves ownership before inserting the copper. A saved phase can claim an implicit same-net connection when its copper joins the endpoints, leaving uncovered connections for later routing.

The four inline repros now check successful replay. The default-router case saves and replays the same routes. Two focused tests cover phase ownership through a plated pad and cross-net rejection. The existing saved fanout tests exercise the separate escape and handoff behavior.

This builds on the coverage in #5614 and targets the merged repros on `main`.

title: test: add inline TSX repros for saved routing phases
description: Adds four small TSX reproductions for the saved-phase bug in 5614, providing tests for various routing scenarios that previously resulted in errors during autorouting.
body:
Adds four small TSX reproductions for the saved-phase bug in #5614. Each test contains the whole board, uses three or four test points, and has a PCB snapshot. The replay examples put the literal paths on `<autoroutingphase pcbTracePaths={...} />`.

- **Save across connections.** The default autorouter routes logical A–B and B–C connections through pad C. Both traces are present on the PCB, but the phase event has no saved paths.
- **Shared pad.** Saved A–B and A–C paths both start at A. Replay reports a duplicate path and emits zero traces.
- **T-junction.** A saved path from C touches the middle of the A–B trace. Replay requires another pad at the end and emits zero traces.
- **Trunk.** An internal segment joins the middle of A–B to the middle of C–D. Replay requires the trunk to start at a pad and emits zero traces.

All four tests reproduce the current behavior on `main`. On #5614, the three replay boards restored two, two, and three traces with no autorouting errors. The export board produced two saved paths, and replaying them preserved the coordinates, widths, and layers of the original copper.

This is a standalone reproduction PR for the cases discussed in #5613.

title: Reuse the rendered Drawing view when switching package tabs
description: Reduces model download time by reusing the rendered Drawing view when switching tabs, preventing unnecessary model downloads and improving performance.
body:
Returning to Drawing currently starts another model download and render, which took about 37 seconds for Classic F1 in a profiled browser run. The PCB and 3D tabs already preserve their expensive viewers between tab changes.

Use that same KeepMountedView mechanism for Drawing. It mounts on first use and retains the rendered sheet and loaded model URLs when another tab is active. Its existing release/build identity pattern resets the viewer when either changes.

Stacked on #6008. This fix removes the expected-failure marker and changes the return-to-Drawing snapshot from a loading message to the completed sheet. The test stalls subsequent model downloads, verifies the original image remains connected, and checks that no additional models were requested. The second regression verifies lazy loading and selected-build invalidation.

This is an in-page cache implemented with the existing viewer lifecycle. It requires no new DrawingViewer prop, global cache, dependency bump, or additional Classic F1 build.

A local browser check also used the full published Classic F1 circuit (3,570 elements) and all 27 unique model files. Returning to Drawing took 312 ms, retained the original image element, and made zero additional model requests, with further model downloads blocked.

Validation:

- `bunx playwright test playwright-tests/package-drawing-cache1.spec.ts playwright-tests/package-drawing-cache2.spec.ts playwright-tests/package-drawing-view.spec.ts --retries=0 --workers=1` — all 6 tests passed, including desktop and mobile navigation.
- `bun test` — 430 passed, 5 existing skips.
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run lint`

Removing the marker was verified to fail specifically because the original drawing image was detached.

description: Optimizes search functionality by incorporating package codes into the text index, reducing candidate results and improving search speed.
body:

Stacked on #463.

`TwoPinComponentHasInvertedRails` currently flags valid TI layouts when only one terminal is connected to a rail. Restrict the warning to a component whose explicitly positive-supply terminal is below its ground terminal.

- Positive supply ↔ ground: retain the inversion check.
- Positive supply ↔ signal: accept either vertical direction.
- Signal ↔ ground: accept either vertical direction.
- Unknown polarity or conflicting power/ground metadata: keep skipping inversion warnings.

The change removes the supply-to-signal resistor branch and the signal-to-ground passive branch. It uses the existing typed metadata and connectivity, adds no Circuit JSON properties or name-based exceptions, and leaves the horizontal-orientation rule unchanged.

The two TI repro fixtures are unchanged; their expected findings become zero. Existing regressions and their analysis snapshots are updated to remove the same false positives. The Allwinner fixture still reports all 47 positive-supply-to-ground inversions, while its 20 single-rail warnings disappear.

**TI references — cropped to the relevant components**

**1. Positive supply ↔ ground: keep the inversion check.** C3–C7 have `730_VBUS` above and GND below. Reversing these terminals still warns when the supply is explicitly identified as positive.

![TI TPS25751EVM: C3–C7 with the positive supply above and ground below](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d79acf5-7376-4663-9ccf-cf7b7770b3e6)

Source: [TI TPS25751EVM user's guide, SLVUCP9B, Figure 5-1, page 39](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=39).

**2. Positive supply ↔ signal: accept either vertical direction.** R13–R18 have their signal terminals above and the shared `730_LDO_3V3` supply below. This is the pull-up bank reproduced in #463.

![TI TPS25751EVM: R13–R18 signal terminals above the shared positive supply](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d59c542c-2421-4141-a67d-1b3b2a656091)

Source: [TI TPS25751EVM user's guide, SLVUCP9B, Figure 5-1, page 39](https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvucp9b/slvucp9b.pdf#page=39).

**3. Signal ↔ ground: accept either vertical direction.** R26 (60.4 Ω) has GND above its signal terminal; R25 (60.4 Ω) has GND below. Both are input terminations. This is the exact circuit used by the second repro in #463.

![TI THS4541RGT EVM: R26 with ground above its signal terminal and R25 with ground below](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/85feea51-0697-4ef8-9cc6-005186e8142c)

title: ci: run bun test as 6 parallel shards balanced by recorded timings
description: This PR modifies the CI workflow to run tests in parallel across 6 shards based on recorded timings, significantly reducing the total test execution time from 55 minutes to approximately 13.5 minutes for the critical path.
body:
The `test` workflow ran every test file in one job, so each PR waited ~55 min. This PR splits it into a 6-job matrix, using the same approach as `tscircuit-autorouter`'s `bun-test.yml`.

## How it works
- `scripts/generate-balanced-test-plan.ts` (ported from the autorouter) reads `test-timings.json` and spreads the test files across shards with longest-first greedy bin packing, writing `.bun-test-plan/testplans/testplanN.txt`. A new file with no recorded timing is costed at the p90.
- `scripts/record-test-timings.ts` rebuilds `test-timings.json` from the per-file `##[group]` markers in a CI run's logs: `bun scripts/record-test-timings.ts <run-id> [...]`.
- `test-timings.json` was seeded from two green `main` runs (44086963002, 44042446919). It covers all 237 files, 55.7 min in total.
- Each shard runs `bun test <files> --timeout 120000`, the same flags as before.
- Superseded PR runs are now cancelled (`main` runs are not), and snapshot diffs are uploaded when a shard fails.
- `test-timings.json` is excluded from the Biome format check because it is generated.

## Expected plan (6 shards)
```
testplan1:   1 files, 13.47 min   <- tests/repros/mt8395-core-full-routing.test.ts
testplan2:  24 files,  8.45 min
testplan3:  25 files,  8.45 min
testplan4:  25 files,  8.45 min
testplan5:  24 files,  8.45 min
testplan6: 138 files,  8.45 min
critical path 13.47 min (was ~55 min)
```
I checked locally that the plans cover all 237 test files exactly once, with no duplicates.

`mt8395-core-full-routing` is one test that solves 138 DDR signals, so it sets the floor. Adding more shards would not lower the wall time unless that test is split.

## Benchmark effect
None. This PR only changes CI: no solver, routing, fixture or benchmark-input code is touched, and the same test files run with the same flags. The `AM3352 benchmark (11/11)` Blacksmith workflow is unchanged.

## Kit boxes: UV laser and UPC sticker

- **New UV laser bench** on the east wall, next to the 3D printers and the label printer: a [ComMarker Omni X](https://store.commarker.com/products/omni-x-uv-laser-engraver) with the slide extension.
  - It engraves "Made in China" on the **base** of 4 blank mailers per run. The boxes lie upside down, 2 across and 2 deep, on the 250 × 400 mm slide.
  - A run takes 20 s of framing plus 12 s per box.
  - The operator unloads a finished run, loads and starts the next, and carries the engraved boxes to the pack-out stacks, the same way plates go from the printers.
  - The shift starts with 12 engraved boxes at pack-out, a finished run on the slide, and the rest blank.
  - The batch run fits laser trips in between benches, and waits for the last run before pack-out if needed.
  - In game mode, press E at the laser bench or on its circle. The control panel has **Engraving done** and **Engrave boxes, take them to pack-out**.
- **Pack-out:**
  - A MUNBYN thermal printer prints the 2 × 1" UPC-A sticker (884400898623, from `tscircuit/product-packaging`).
  - The operator tips the box over and puts the sticker on a corner of the base, beside the engraving and about 8 mm from both edges.
  - Pack-out stops with a message if a unit's box hasn't been engraved yet.
- The bare-unit line has neither the laser nor the UPC printer.

## Carton labels

- The label printer prints the FBA box ID and then a 4 × 6" DHL carrier label. The DHL label is a marked sample showing ship-from, ship-to the fulfillment center, the FBA shipment ID as reference, piece count, weight and tracking bars.
- Both are carried to ship-ready and applied so the carrier label never covers the box ID:
  - **Kit carton:** side by side on the front.
  - **Bag carton (10 × 8 × 6"):** the carrier label goes on the back, because the front can't fit both.
- Cartons get a `carrierLabelSpot`. The label printer holds its sheets while either carton label is printing.

## Camera and scenarios

- The camera's target, distance and angles move on critically damped springs, so a close-up change glides there instead of cutting:
  - Each move starts from rest and settles without overshoot.
  - Long bench-to-bench moves pull back a little on the way.
  - Dragging to orbit takes over at once.
- Removes the "Walk the floor" and "Pick up the screwdriver" scenarios and the patrol route. The F key still picks up the screwdriver in game mode.

- `bun test` passes (40). New tests cover:

- **Laser model:** 4 boxes per run assumes the 12 W Omni X with the slide. The 6 W slide fits 2 per run.
